Process — procedures the system walks for you

Draw a recovery plan, post-upgrade validation or runbook as a diagram of checks, gates and actions, and let SATOM walk it step by step — as a harmless rehearsal or, when armed, for real.

What is it?#

A process is a procedure drawn as a diagram: each step asks a question of the running system (is this URL healthy? does this appliance grade OK?) or performs an action, and the arrows say where to go depending on the answer. SATOM walks the diagram and reports which step stopped it. The same shape covers a disaster-recovery plan, a post-upgrade validation, an onboarding check and an incident runbook.

What does it do?#

  • Lets you draw steps and arrows in an editor and validates the diagram before it can be saved.
  • Walks the diagram on demand, against one chosen appliance when steps need one.
  • Runs as a rehearsal by default — nothing is written — or armed when you tick Arm this run.
  • Parks on a Manual gate until a person answers, even hours later.
  • Keeps every run with its own copy of the diagram it walked, its steps and a verdict, and since 3.4.0 what started it (trigger_key: the finding, the scheduled action or the API token).
  • Starts, since 3.4.0, from an event of the integration-hook catalogue, from the scheduled action "Walk a process", or from the API — as a rehearsal unless each door is explicitly armed.
  • Undoes what a walk wrote with a Compensate step, newest first, only for steps that recorded an inverse.
  • Imports and exports processes as XML files.

NAF block: Orchestrator. A process coordinates checks, gates, catalogue actions and hooks and never touches an appliance itself — the writes it schedules are the catalogue's; see Where SATOM sits in the NAF Framework.

Requirements#

  • For steps that act on a device (console read, appliance health, collect diagnostics, console script, and catalogue actions that need a target): a registered appliance visible in the current ADOM.
  • For DNS check without an explicit server: an enabled DNS server in Settings.
  • For Integration hook steps: a hook defined under Integrations and the satom-integrations runner enabled on this node.

Permissions#

Action Permission
See the process list, a diagram, its runs, Export XML any key granting the legacy view, e.g. operations.view
Create, edit, delete, draw and save, import, Run now, answer a gate any key granting the legacy config_write, e.g. operations.apply

A user without config_write sees the diagram read-only and the note "Running a process needs the config_write permission."

Where the menu entry is. Users with users.manage find Process in the Administrator sidebar group. Every other user who can view the page finds it in a sidebar group of its own, Automation → Process.

ADOM visibility. A process is offered in the ADOMs ticked under Offer this process in. With no ADOM ticked it is a draft (draft — no ADOM) and appears only in the Global console. The Global console sees every process. A process not offered in the current ADOM answers 404. Runs follow their process's ADOM: the run page, answering a waiting Manual gate (resume) and the Recent runs list on the index cover only runs of processes offered in the current ADOM.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: process runs (run page, resume, Recent runs) follow their process's ADOM; before, a run from another ADOM could be opened and resumed by its id and appeared in Recent runs. Operators and read-only users now see Process in the sidebar (Automation group); before, only administrators did.

How to use#

Create a process#

  1. Open Administrator → Process (or Automation → Process) and press New process.
  2. Fill in Key (lowercase letters, digits, - or _; cannot be changed later), Name, Description, the ADOMs under Offer this process in and Enabled.
  3. Save. The process opens with a single Start step.

Draw the diagram#

  1. In Diagram, use Add a step to add steps (see the table below).
  2. Click a step to edit its label and parameters in Selected step.
  3. Use Connect to draw an arrow and choose its outcome: always, pass, fail or unknown.
  4. Delete selected removes a step or arrow; Fit re-centres the view.
  5. Press Save diagram. An invalid diagram is refused whole, with the reasons listed.
Step What it asks Writes?
Start Where the walk begins — exactly one per process no
End A terminal point, with an optional Closing note no
Decision Did an earlier step (Step key) end as pass / fail / unknown? no
Manual gate Stops and waits for a person (Ask the operator) no
HTTP check URL, Expect status (200), Slower than (ms) fails (0 = off), Body must contain, Timeout (s) (10) no
TCP check Host or IP, Port, Timeout (s) (3); keeps refused apart from timeout no
DNS check Name, Server (blank = first enabled server), Answer must contain no
Console read One read-only CLI Command on the appliance, with Output must contain / Output must NOT contain no
Appliance health The Monitoring grade; Worst acceptable ok / warn / crit no
Collect diagnostics Runs the read-only SSH battery and saves the transcript on this node no
Catalogue action An action from the scheduled-actions catalog yes, when armed
Console script CLI lines sent to the appliance (Commands, On error, Disruptive only on) yes, when armed
Integration hook Queues one hook and waits for its verdict (Hook, Payload (JSON object), Wait for the result) yes, when armed
Compensate (3.4.0) Undoes what the earlier steps of this walk wrote, newest first: a status a catalogue action flipped, an Observatory fix, a provisioning run. A write that recorded no inverse is listed as unknown, never guessed; a write that failed is never replayed. Unarmed, it lists what it would undo yes, when armed

Arrows. An explicit outcome wins over always. A step may have only one arrow per outcome, so a run is always in exactly one place. Loops are allowed; a walk is aborted after 200 executed steps.

Run a process#

  1. On the process page, in Walk this process, choose the Appliance if the diagram has device steps.
  2. Tick Arm this run to let write steps act. Leave it unticked for a rehearsal. (On a diagram that only reads, arming is dropped automatically — "Every step in this diagram only reads.")
  3. Press Run now. The run page opens with the steps, their outcomes and output.
  4. If the run stops on a Manual gate (This run is waiting for you), read the prompt, optionally fill Note (recorded on the step), and press Passed or Failed. The walk continues along the matching arrow.

Start a process from an event, a schedule or the API#

Three doors besides Run now, added in 3.4.0. Each is a rehearsal unless it is armed on its own: arming the Run button never arms a trigger.

From an event. On the process form choose a Trigger event from the integration-hook catalogue (alert.fired, upgrade.failed, change.approved …) and narrow it with the filter fields — ADOM, appliances, alert family and a severity floor. When such an event is noticed, the walk is queued as a job; it never runs inside the alert evaluation or the hook dispatch that noticed it. Three rules bound a storm, and every refusal is kept as a run with status skipped and its reason:

  • one running instance per process and appliance;
  • Runs per hour, at most (default 10) per process;
  • rehearsal, unless Arm triggered walks is ticked — the form says in red what that means: SATOM writes to a device with nobody at the screen.

A finding that started a walk owes the alert cooldown; one that was skipped does not. Device findings carry the appliance id, so the trigger can point the walk at the device that raised it.

From a schedule. Create the Walk a process action under Automations with the process key and, if the diagram writes, its armed parameter. An armed walk of a writing diagram runs only bound to an approved change request. The action is flagged dangerous, so the generic /api/v1/actions door never runs it.

From the API. POST /api/v1/processes/<id>/run with the appliance and "armed": false by default; "armed": true needs the explicit process_arm capability on the token. GET /api/v1/processes lists what the token's ADOM may see and GET /api/v1/process-runs/<id> returns a run with its steps. See REST API.

Import or export XML#

  • Export XML on a process page downloads process-<key>.xml.
  • Process → Import XML loads a file. If the key already exists, type the key in Replace an existing process to replace its steps, arrows and settings; run history is kept either way.
<satom-process key="dr-failover-check" name="DR failover check" enabled="yes">
  <description>Prove the standby answers before anyone is told it does.</description>
  <adoms><adom>fortiweb</adom></adoms>
  <steps>
    <step key="start" kind="start" label="Start" x="60" y="40"/>
    <step key="vip" kind="tcp_check" label="VIP answers" x="60" y="140">
      <param name="host">192.0.2.10</param>
      <param name="port">443</param>
    </step>
    <step key="ok" kind="end" label="Standby is serving" x="60" y="240"/>
  </steps>
  <arrows>
    <arrow from="start" to="vip" branch="always"/>
    <arrow from="vip" to="ok" branch="pass"/>
  </arrows>
</satom-process>

Rules: every parameter is an element (never an attribute), so multi-line scripts survive; no <adom> makes the process a draft; an ADOM this installation does not have is an error; the file is accepted whole or refused whole and passes the same validator as the editor. draw.io, BPMN and Visio files are recognised and refused by name. Maximum file size 1 MB.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Key Permanent identifier, lowercase letters, digits, -, _ Yes dr-failover-check
Name Display name Yes DR failover check
Description Free text No —
Offer this process in ADOMs that list it; none = draft No FortiWeb
Enabled A disabled process cannot run ("This process is disabled.") No ticked
Trigger event (3.4.0) An event of the integration-hook catalogue that starts a walk; blank = manual, scheduled or API only No alert.fired
Trigger filter (3.4.0) ADOM, appliance ids, alert family and severity floor the event must match No family device, severity critical
Arm triggered walks (3.4.0) Off = every triggered walk is a rehearsal. On = SATOM writes with nobody at the screen (the form says so in red) No off
Runs per hour, at most (3.4.0) Budget of triggered walks per process; refusals are kept as skipped runs No 10

Example#

🧪Example — Post-upgrade validation with a human check

Start → HTTP check https://192.0.2.10/healthz expect 200 → (pass) Appliance health worst acceptable warn → (pass) Manual gate "Log in to the application and confirm the order page loads" → (pass) End Validated. Each fail arrow leads to End Escalate. Run it against fweb-01 without arming — none of these steps writes, so arming would be dropped anyway.

Result#

A run ends with a Verdict:

Verdict Meaning
ok Every step that ran passed
failed At least one step failed, or the walk was aborted (for example after 200 steps)
partial Nothing failed, but some steps ended unknown — "Nothing failed, but N step(s) could not be looked at. This is a partial walk, not a clean bill of health."

Step outcomes are pass, fail, unknown (SATOM could not look: no appliance, SSH refused, not armed) and skipped ("not reached — an earlier step stopped this path"). A branch the plan deliberately did not take is not listed as skipped.

In a rehearsal, a Catalogue action runs as a real dry run and its row says rehearsed (not armed); a Console script and an Integration hook are not sent at all and end unknown — a rehearsal stops where the repair would have been.

Runs survive editing and deletion of the process: each keeps the name, key and diagram it walked. Create, edit, delete, save diagram, run, resume, import and export are written to the audit log (process.*).

Troubleshooting#

"This diagram cannot run yet: …"#

Possible causes — the saved diagram fails validation, for example "A process needs exactly one Start step (found 0).", "Step 'x' has 2 arrows for the same outcome (pass). …" or "Step 'x' needs URL."

Solution — fix the named step or arrow in the editor and Save diagram.

"This process has steps that act on a device — choose one."#

Solution — pick an Appliance before pressing Run now.

"A process with the key 'x' already exists. To replace it — its steps, its arrows and its settings — type its key in the confirmation box. …"#

Solution — type the key in Replace an existing process, or change the key in the file.

"This installation has no ADOM 'x'. It has: …"#

Solution — edit the <adom> elements of the file to ADOMs this installation has, or remove them to import as a draft.

An Integration hook step ends "unknown"#

Possible causes — the run was not armed ("not armed — hook 'x' was NOT queued"), the hook no longer exists, the payload is not a JSON object, or the request was still queued when the wait ran out because the integrations runner on this node did not pick it up.

Solution — arm the run; check the hook under Integrations; check that satom-integrations.path is enabled on this node.

Advanced#

Advanced The Console script write door

A Console script applies the operator console's own rules, abbreviations included (exe reb counts as a reboot, set passw as a password change, and exe fa is refused like a factory reset): wiping or reformatting commands are refused when you save, at any permission level; disruptive commands (reboot, shutdown, restore, HA changes, password changes) require Disruptive only on to name the one appliance, and at run time the run must be pointed at exactly that appliance or the step sends nothing; the whole script is checked before the session opens; with On error 1 the first failure stops the rest. Everything sent is audited under the same name the Console page uses, marked as coming from a process. The object-delete guard of the web UI does not see a delete inside a CLI config block.

Advanced Execution model

A run started with Run now is walked inside the web request that starts it. A run started by an event or by the Walk a process action is queued as a job and walked by the job runner, never inside the scheduler's cycle. A manual gate saves the run's position as one step key, so answering it later resumes from the saved snapshot of the diagram, not from the current definition; the inverse a writing step recorded travels with the step, so a walk resumed after a gate still knows what to compensate. An Integration hook step writes a request file for the unprivileged runner and waits at most the hook's own timeout.

Catalogue actions that require an approved change request (upgrade, reboot, HA failover) are not offered — a process is a plan, not an approval.
